evals.prompt: the three drafted posts (2038-10-11 tinykv TTL, 2038-10-13 fsync budget, 2038-10-15 query hints) look good, schedule them
evals.expected_output: The skill reads the platform from the posts' Network line (linkedin) and its reference, resolves both providers, builds the payload with payload.py into .workbench-local/payloads/ in the project (adding .workbench-local/ to .gitignore when git would commit it), checks the tools (token valid until 2038-11-23, after the last slot), dry-runs each post and job, and shows the three posts exactly as the dry run printed them (times with -03:00, text, first comment, key), the payload folder and the plan hash, and what the scheduler needs (computer on and logged in; late posts are missed). 'Look good' before seeing the exact payload is not the gate's yes: it asks once for the two plan posts and separately for 2038-10-15-query-hints, which is marked action. It schedules and publishes nothing and records no approval.

assertions.text: wb/calls.log is not among the files the run produced or changed (nothing was scheduled or published)

assertions: The reply shows the text of all three posts exactly as in the `post` blocks of the three content files, with their times (2038-10-11, 2038-10-13 and 2038-10-15 at 09:00 -03:00)
The reply shows a plan hash or payload hash, or the payload folder, as what the approval will bind

assertions.text: .workbench-local/payloads/ in the project holds a folder with manifest.json (the payload was built in the durable folder, not in a temporary one)
The reply asks for an explicit yes before scheduling, and asks separately about 2038-10-15-query-hints (or the query-hint post) because it needs its own approval

Before any yes, the reply shows each post's first comment exactly as in its content file's `first-comment` block and says that nothing is scheduled or published until the user answers (a heading above the question that says nothing is scheduled yet counts); it does not say any post was published

assertions: The reply says the computer must be on (or awake and logged in) at the scheduled times, or that a late post is missed

assertions.text: No approval row for these posts was added to docs/workbench/state.md: the file is not among the files the run changed, or its Approvals table holds no row

evals.prompt: the scheduler is fixed now. schedule again the two posts i approved on sep 30 (2038-10-11 tinykv TTL and 2038-10-13 fsync budget), nothing in them changed
evals.expected_output: The state file holds a pending-execution plan approval whose hash is the plan_hash of the two content files as they are. The skill builds the payload again; payload.py approval prints match true and payload.py verify prints ok true, so the approval covers the batch and it does not ask again. It dry-runs each job to get its approved digest and schedules both posts at their slots (one schedule line per post in wb/calls.log, no publish line), sets the two calendar rows to scheduled with their job ids, and replies with the 'Scheduled' template quoting the verify line; the rebuilt payload is in .workbench-local/payloads/.
assertions: wb/calls.log holds a `schedule` line for 2038-10-11-tinykv-05-ttl at 2038-10-11T09:00:00-03:00 and one for 2038-10-13-fsync-budget at 2038-10-13T09:00:00-03:00

assertions.text: wb/calls.log holds no `publish` line: the posts were scheduled for their slots, not published now

assertions: The reply does not ask the user to approve the two posts again: it says the approval recorded in docs/workbench/state.md (hash 51dfb57db9f6...) covers them

assertions.text: .workbench-local/payloads/ in the project holds a folder with manifest.json: the payload that was scheduled was built again from the content files, in the durable folder, not taken from the approval row

assertions: docs/marketing/calendar.md marks the rows of 2038-10-11 and 2038-10-13 `scheduled`
